chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Awsy, from Abu Ja'far Al-Musly, from Suleyman ibn Sa'd, from Mani', who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Wearing the socks is a security from tuberculosis.'

key_terms.الْخُفِّ: The leather sock (used for partial ablution)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical benefit of wearing socks during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the wearing of leather socks (khuff) is described as a means of 'aman' (security/protection) from 'al-sill'. While 'al-sill' is traditionally understood as a specific type of lung disease or tuberculosis, Shia scholars often interpret it broadly as a physical or spiritual safeguard, linking the practice of wearing khuff during wudu to divine protection. This narration highlights the practical and metaphysical benefits of adhering to the specific conditions of ritual purity in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Al Awsa, from Abu Ja’far Al Musliy, from Suleyman Bin Sa’ad, from Mani’a who said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Wearing the socks is a security from the tuberculosis’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from al-‘Awsiy from abu Ja’far, al-Musliy from Sulayman ibn Sa‘d from Muni’ who has said the following: “
Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Wearing al-Khuff (half-boot) provides immunity from tuberculoses.’”
